title_en: The first words of revelation: the command to read
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The occasions of revelation (who the persons were, what happened) are not in the verses; they appear only under unknowns and uncertainties, as later tradition, with the hadith to add later. Pronouns the Arabic leaves open are left open. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The passage opens with a command to read in the name of the Lord of the one addressed, who created.
God created the human being from an alaq, a word often rendered a clinging thing or a clot.
The command to read is repeated, with the statement that the Lord of the one addressed is the most generous.
God is the one who taught by the pen and taught the human being what he did not know.

chapters.summary_md: The passage opens with a command to read in the name of the Lord who created [c1]. It says that He created the human being from an alaq [c2], that He is the most generous [c3], and that He taught by the pen and taught the human being what he did not know [c4].
chapters.body_md:
The passage opens with a command to read in the name of the Lord of the one addressed, who created [c1].

It says that God created the human being from an alaq, a word often rendered a clinging thing or a clot [c2]. The command to read is then repeated, with the statement that the Lord of the one addressed is the most generous [c3].

The passage ends by saying that God is the one who taught by the pen and taught the human being what he did not know [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The command to read is given without saying what is to be read [c1]. The passage joins creation [c2], generosity [c3] and teaching by the pen [c4] to one and the same Lord [c1]. The word alaq is kept in Arabic here because it is read in more than one way [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The passage tells us to read in the name of our Lord, who created [c1]. It says that God taught by the pen [c4]. It says that God taught the human being what he did not know [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage ties reading and learning to the name of the Lord who created [c1][c4]. Another is that what a human being comes to know is presented as something God taught [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: that these verses are the first revelation. The inventory title calls them traditionally the first; the verses themselves do not say so.
- Not established: when, where or how these words came, who spoke them to the one addressed, or who the one addressed is. The verses name no one.
- Not established: what the one addressed was to read. The verse gives no object.
- The Arabic alaq is read in more than one way; this draft keeps the Arabic word beside a common rendering and decides nothing.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the occasion, the place and the circumstances in which these verses came. None is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the beginning of revelation and on the occasion of these ayat, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.
Whether these verses were the first to be revealed is a matter of later tradition; the inventory title says so with the word traditionally. A scholar should decide how the page words this.
The sense of alaq is for the reviewer; the draft gives a common rendering and the Arabic word.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
